titleStmt.title: Cognitive Radio Spectrum Sensing and Jamming Cancellation via Oblique Projection and GLRT

analytic.title: Cognitive Radio Spectrum Sensing and Jamming Cancellation via Oblique Projection and GLRT

abstract.p: In this paper, we propose Oblique Projection-Based Jamming Cancellation (OPJC) combined with the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) for robust spectrum sensing in cognitive radio networks. We formulate the signal model in multi-dimensional subspaces derived from linear algebra and covariance matrices. Under intentional adversarial jamming, oblique projection operators separate the desired signal subspace from the interference subspace. The detection performance is analyzed using binary hypothesis testing.

div.head: 1. Introduction
div.p: Cognitive Radio enables opportunistic spectrum access for secondary users by dynamically monitoring frequency bands through Spectrum Sensing [1]. However, Physical Layer Security is severely threatened when adversarial jammers emit high-power interference. Jamming Cancellation is essential to maintain communication reliability.

div.head: 2. Preliminaries and System Model
div.p: Foundations in Linear Algebra and vector Subspaces provide the structural basis for modern signal processing. Consider an N-dimensional complex space decomposed into signal subspace S and interference subspace R.
The sample covariance matrix of the received observation vector is computed from statistical expectations:
An Oblique Projection operator E_sr projects along the interference subspace R onto the signal subspace S:

formula.latex: E_{sr} = S (S^H P_R^\perp S)^{-1} S^H P_R^\perp

div.formula: E_{sr} = S (S^H P_R^\perp S)^{-1} S^H P_R^\perp
div.p: Here P_R denotes the Orthogonal Projection operator onto subspace R, and E_sr removes all jamming components while preserving signal structure.

div.head: 3. Detection via Hypothesis Testing and GLRT
div.p: Spectrum sensing is formulated as binary Hypothesis Testing between null hypothesis H0 (idle channel) and alternative hypothesis H1 (primary user active). Because noise variance is unknown, we derive the GLRT decision statistic:
The GLRT detector achieves optimal asymptotic detection probability under generalized likelihood ratio criteria [2].

div.head: 4. Proposed Methodology: Oblique Projection-Based Jamming Cancellation
div.p: We propose Oblique Projection-Based Jamming Cancellation (OPJC). Jamming cancellation is achieved via oblique projection operator E_sr by nulling the interference subspace prior to evaluating the GLRT statistic. This eliminates interference while ensuring full detection sensitivity.
